conservation.notes: A common and adaptable species with a stable population; sometimes exploited for the pet trade.

human_tolerance.notes: Not a forest species, but in the forest zone it is still found in degraded habitats and towns, including gardens, where it shelters by day in sand, under stones and in debris.

phases.name: breeding
phases.note: German Wikipedia: calling and breeding activity runs from February to November and is highest in early spring; males that are calling are territorial towards other males.

phases.name: dormancy
phases.note: In the driest and coolest weeks the toad stays hidden in sand or under stones and calls stop.

vocalizations.description: The calling male gives a short, harsh croak in bursts from the edge of water or a shallow pool; calling runs from February to November and is loudest in early spring, and males answer one another and hold ground against newcomers.

conservation.note: 'A common species across most of its wide range ... the population is stable so the International Union for Conservation of Nature has listed its conservation status as being of least concern'; it has sometimes been exploited for the pet trade.

range.note: Country list taken from the article's distribution sentence, which names Ghana and the countries from Senegal to Uganda, plus the oases in Algeria and Libya and northern Egypt.

traits.limb_count.note: Four legs with webbed hind feet.

traits.locomotion_modes.note: The article describes a bouncing movement, walking and movement through water with webbed hind feet.

traits.nest_type.note: Eggs are laid in water near rivers; Ground is the schema's nearest class for a spawning site with no nest structure.

traits.mass_kg.note: No open source gives a mass for this species, and the schema requires the field. 0.04 kg is an authored estimate for a toad of 9-13 cm, roughly a quarter of the 0.165 kg the common toad (Bufo bufo) in this kit carries at 15 cm. Treat it as an estimate.

traits.length_m.note: Midpoint of 9-13 cm, where females are noticeably larger than males.

traits.lifespan_y.note: No published longevity figure for this species; 10 years is a judgement close to the common toad's 11 years in this kit.

traits.diet.note: Authored: like other bufonids the species takes invertebrates; no open source gives diet shares for it.

traits.social.note: Males hold ground against other males at the calling site; outside breeding the animal is solitary, and the bounds are authored.

traits.activity_pattern.note: German Wikipedia calls the species crepuscular and notes that it hides by day in sand or under stones; calling is a night activity from February to November.

traits.defense.note: 'When threatened, they would bounce to confuse (or escape) predators', which is the freeze-and-hop escape the shared anuran program runs.

traits.wariness.note: Authored: it is found in towns and gardens.

habitat.use.note: A ground animal of savanna, farmland and degraded town habitat that shelters in sand and stones and goes to water to breed.

habitat.shelter_tag.note: Hides by day in sand, under stones or similarly.

habitat.resources.note: Invertebrate prey is authored from the bufonid diet; burrow from the daytime hiding places; water and pond from 'often found near rivers, where it also breeds'.

habitat.human_tolerance.note: 'In the forest zone it can still be found in degraded habitats and towns (including gardens)'; light_max authored.

seasonal.strategy.note: German Wikipedia gives activity through the year with a summer dry-season lull in calling; the species is not a hibernator.

seasonal.phases.note: The February to November calling and breeding window and the daytime hiding behaviour are from the German article; the December to January phase name stands for the quiet period.

seasonal.life_stages.note: Authored: eggs and tadpoles in water, then a short metamorphosis and a growing juvenile period.

vocalizations.croak.note: The February to November calling season, its early-spring peak and the territorial behaviour of calling males are from the German article; the description of the call itself is limited to what that source states.

look.note: Authored: an olive-brown toad with darker markings and the pale line along the flank typical of the genus; block proportions authored.

behavior.note: The shared nocturnal-anuran program fits a toad that hides by day and calls at night; call_m1 and call_m2 are set to the February to November calling season the German article gives.
